headline: Benchmarks and simulations test inference tools for selection and ancient DNA imputation
label: Population Genomic Inference Methods
summary: Growing ancient and Neolithic genome datasets make direct benchmarking of local ancestry and imputation tools testable against selection inference.
synthesis: The dominant thread is the evaluation of population genomic inference methods applied to human variation shaped by selection and demographic history. A benchmark of eight local ancestry inference methods on 176 imputed Neolithic genomes recommends Gnomix or RFMix and tests selection signals at FADS1/2. A coalescent and simulation analysis of ancient DNA imputation reference panels finds that a joint 1000 Genomes-ancient panel modestly aids rare-variant imputation. A genomic history study of Roman and early medieval Britain addresses historical processes shaping fine-scale diversity in that population. A structural variation map across 460 phased HLA assemblies links structural haplotypes to expression differences, a locus-level study adjacent to this methodological work rather than an evaluation of inference tools. What is new is explicit simulation- or benchmark-based assessment of inference tools applied to ancient and historical genomes.
